about.title: Coalinga Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: A fall can happen in seconds — a wet floor at a store off E Polk Street, an unmarked step near Forest Avenue, or uneven pavement outside a business along E Elm Avenue — but the aftermath often lingers for weeks or months. Coalinga is a small, close-knit community, and many of its shops, apartment complexes, and public buildings see steady foot traffic, which means property owners carry an ongoing duty to keep walkways reasonably safe. Under California law, a property owner or manager isn't automatically responsible just because someone fell; the injured person generally has to show the owner knew, or should have known, about the hazard and didn't fix it or warn about it in time. That's why documenting what caused the fall, and getting to any surveillance footage before it's deleted, matters so much. LawProactive doesn't handle claims directly — we connect you, free of charge, with an independent attorney who can evaluate what happened and explain your options.

whyChoose.title: Why Documentation Matters in a Coalinga Fall Case

items.title: Notice Has to Be Shown
items.desc: California law generally requires proof the property owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard and failed to address it. Photos of the condition, timestamps, and witness accounts help build that picture.

items.title: Surveillance Footage Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many Coalinga businesses overwrite security video within days or weeks. An attorney can send a preservation request quickly so this evidence isn't lost before it's ever reviewed.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Erase, a Claim
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning even if you're found partly responsible for the fall, you may still recover a percentage of damages. An independent attorney can help assess how shared fault might apply to your specific situation.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a slip-and-fall claim in Coalinga?
items.answer: In most cases, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit. If the property involved is owned by a public entity — a city building or Fresno County facility, for example — the deadline is much shorter, sometimes just a few months. It's best to speak with an attorney as soon as possible so no deadline is missed.

items.question: What should I do right after falling at a store or business in Coalinga?
items.answer: If you're able, take photos of exactly what caused the fall — a spill, a broken step, poor lighting — before it's cleaned up or fixed. Report the incident to management and ask for a written record, and try to get names of any witnesses. These steps help preserve evidence that supports the notice requirement under California law.

items.question: Does it matter that Coalinga is a smaller city with fewer businesses?
items.answer: Not for your legal rights — the same premises liability standards apply whether the fall happened at a large retailer or a small local shop. What can matter is how quickly surveillance footage gets overwritten or how records are kept, so acting promptly to preserve evidence is important regardless of the business's size.
